AI Pricing Statistics 2026: Models, Price Points and Trends

Explainerlowob research

By lowob · 16 November 2026 · 9-minute read · Revenue

In 2026, 37% of software companies used hybrid pricing (Growth Unhinged, May 2026), consumption pricing reached 42% of AI companies and outcome pricing 23% (ICONIQ, July 2026), and AI product gross margins averaged 45% in 2025. Buyers lean towards metering: 42.9% prefer consumption pricing for GenAI features. Most figures here are surveys run by investors, analysts or vendors.

This page collects the numbers. The analysis of what to do with them is in lowob's pricing hub, Seats, usage or outcomes, and in the explainers on AI gross margin and AI credits. Vendor prices were checked on the vendors' own pages on 16 November 2026, in US dollars.

How reliable are these statistics?

Treat them as directional. Growth Unhinged's survey was supported by Metronome, a billing vendor, and is self-reported. ICONIQ and Bessemer are investors, and their 2026 and 2027 margins are projections. Futurum did not disclose fielding dates in its release. Gartner's figures are forecasts. Vendor prices are list prices and change often; negotiated prices are usually lower. Where sellers and buyers disagree, as on outcome pricing, both can be true: more vendors offer it while fewer buyers say they prefer it.

lowob takeaways

  • Hybrid is the norm. Most AI companies combine a fixed fee with usage, credits or outcomes.
  • Buyers want metering for AI. Preference for outcome pricing on GenAI features is falling.
  • Margins sit below SaaS. Investor data puts AI products at about 25% to 60%.
  • Date every price. Units and list prices changed at several large vendors in 2026.

Common questions

What percentage of AI companies use usage-based pricing?

ICONIQ's July 2026 survey of about 300 AI executives found consumption-based pricing at 42%, up from 35% six months earlier. Deloitte cited a Maxio survey finding 83% of AI-native SaaS companies offer usage-based pricing. The figures measure different things: ICONIQ counts the model in use, Maxio whether it is offered at all.

How many software companies use hybrid pricing in 2026?

Kyle Poyar's Growth Unhinged survey of more than 230 software companies, published in May 2026, found 37% use a hybrid pricing model, up from 25% a year earlier. ICONIQ separately found AI companies blend an average of 1.7 pricing models. The survey was supported by Metronome, a billing vendor, and is self-reported.

What is the average gross margin for AI products?

ICONIQ's July 2026 State of AI report put the average AI product gross margin at 45% in 2025, projected to rise to 53% in 2026 and 59% in 2027. Bessemer's August 2025 report put its fastest-growing AI start-ups at about 25%. SaaS Capital says SaaS licence revenue usually earns 80% to 85%.

Do buyers prefer outcome-based pricing for AI?

Fewer do than a year ago. The Futurum Group's survey of 830 IT decision makers, released in April 2026, found preference for outcome-based GenAI pricing fell from 30.9% to 26.8%, while preference for consumption pricing rose to 42.9%. Futurum linked the fall to uncertainty about how to define and measure AI outcomes.

How much do AI assistants cost per user for business?

As checked on vendors' pages on 16 November 2026, Microsoft 365 Copilot Business lists at $21 per user per month on annual billing, ChatGPT Business and Claude Team standard seats at $20, and Google includes Gemini in Workspace Business Standard at $14. Premium seats at OpenAI and Anthropic cost $100 per seat per month on annual billing.
